summary: Kaigen Outdoor Co., an outdoor apparel brand, signed a master services agreement with Dreisur Fulfillment Services LLC for e-commerce fulfillment, returns processing and peak-season surge services. The MSA's Effective Date is March 1, 2025. The folder holds a DPA, a service level schedule, a parent guaranty from Dreisur's parent, Amendment No. 1 dated June 2, 2026, a September 14, 2026 notice letter from Kaigen announcing that its parent is being sold to Sorrelpeak Capital Partners (expected closing December 15, 2026), and a statement of work. It also holds two distractors, an office lease and a certificate of insurance. Six issues are planted. (1) A long auto-renewal with a narrow opt-out window. (2) A Delaware law and forum clause in the DPA, which the MSA lets prevail for personal data matters. (3) A deemed-assignment change-of-control consent requirement that the notice letter ignores. (4) A narrower 'Peak Season' definition in the controlling SLA Schedule. (5) An uncapped customer-only indemnity. (6) An amendment that deletes the section a cap carve-out points to, which pulls data security breaches under the cap.

issues.label: automatic renewal
issues.description: MSA §12.2 provides that after the three-year Initial Term (F2) the MSA automatically renews for successive three-year Renewal Terms. The only way out is written non-renewal notice given not more than 120 nor fewer than 90 days before the end of the then-current Term, a 30-day window. The MSA gives Kaigen no termination for convenience. If Kaigen misses the window, it is locked into another three years of fulfillment services with Dreisur.
detect_terms: not more than 120 nor fewer than 90 days
issues.expected_finding: MSA §12.2 automatically renews the MSA for successive three-year terms unless Kaigen gives notice in a narrow 30-day window 120 to 90 days before term end, so Kaigen should calendar the window and negotiate shorter renewal terms, a longer opt-out window or a termination-for-convenience right.

issues.label: governing law mismatch
issues.description: Each provision reads as ordinary drafting on its own. DPA §12 provides that the DPA is governed by Delaware law, with exclusive jurisdiction in the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware. MSA §2.3, the order of precedence, provides that in any conflict concerning the Processing of Personal Data the DPA prevails over the MSA, including the MSA's New York law and New York County forum clause in §17.1. Read together, any dispute over a breach of consumer data that Dreisur handles is governed by Delaware law and must be brought in Delaware. All other MSA disputes go to New York. Kaigen faces split proceedings, the risk of inconsistent rulings on the same incident, and an unplanned forum.
detect_terms: laws of the State of Delaware
Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware
issues.expected_finding: The DPA's Delaware law and Delaware forum clause prevails over the MSA's New York law and New York County forum clause for personal-data disputes because of MSA §2.3, which splits Kaigen's claims across two laws and forums, so the DPA should be conformed to New York law and the MSA forum.

issues.label: change of control consent
issues.description: MSA §16.3 deems a Change of Control of a party to be an assignment that requires the other party's prior written consent. It makes any assignment without consent void and lets the non-assigning party terminate. MSA §1.1 defines Change of Control to include an indirect acquisition of more than 50% of the voting securities of any entity that Controls a party. Kaigen's notice letter dated September 14, 2026 (D6) tells Dreisur that Kaigen Group Holdings has agreed to be sold to Sorrelpeak Capital Partners, with closing expected on or about December 15, 2026. The letter states that no action is required by Dreisur and does not request consent. Read together, the closing is a Change of Control of Kaigen that needs Dreisur's consent. Without that consent, Dreisur can treat the deemed assignment as void and terminate the MSA.
issues.section: §16.3 (Assignment; Change of Control) and §1.1 (definition of Change of Control)
issues.expected_finding: The sale of Kaigen Group Holdings to Sorrelpeak, which the September 14, 2026 letter says should close on or about December 15, 2026, is a deemed assignment under MSA §16.3 that requires Dreisur's prior written consent, which the letter did not request, so Kaigen should obtain Dreisur's written consent or waiver before closing to avoid a void assignment and a termination right.

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: MSA §1.1 defines Peak Season as October 15 through January 15, covering the fall and winter outerwear launch and the holiday returns window. The SOW's surge-staffing obligations use that definition. SLA Schedule §1 defines Peak Season as November 20 through December 31. SLA §3 applies enhanced 3x service credits only to failures during that period, and SLA §5 ties the chronic-failure termination right to it. MSA §2.3 ranks the SLA Schedule above the MSA body, so the narrower SLA definition controls the remedies. Read together, Dreisur's service failures from October 15 to November 19 and from January 1 to 15 earn only standard credits and cannot trigger the chronic-failure termination right, even though Dreisur owes surge performance in those weeks.
issues.expected_finding: The SLA Schedule's narrower Peak Season (November 20 through December 31) controls over the MSA's definition (October 15 through January 15) under MSA §2.3, so enhanced credits and the chronic-failure termination right do not cover the early-season and January weeks, and the SLA definition should be conformed to the MSA's.

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: MSA §11.3(a) excludes 'a party's obligations under Section 10' from the liability cap, which looks mutual. MSA §10.1, Dreisur's indemnity, states that Supplier's obligations under this Section 10.1 are subject to Section 11.1, so Dreisur's indemnity stays capped. Kaigen's indemnity in §10.2 has no such limit. It covers any claims arising from Customer Products, including product liability, product recalls, mislabeling, and customs or regulatory fines. Read together, only Kaigen's indemnity is uncapped, so Kaigen bears unlimited exposure for broad product and regulatory risks while Dreisur's indemnity is limited to 12 months' fees.
issues.expected_finding: Because §10.1 subjects Dreisur's indemnity to the cap while §11.3(a) excludes Section 10 obligations from it, only Kaigen's broad §10.2 indemnity for product liability, recalls and customs or regulatory fines is uncapped, so Kaigen should cap its indemnity or make the treatment of both indemnities reciprocal.

issues.label: liability cap carve-out conflict
issues.description: MSA §11.3(b) carves breach of Section 9.2 (Data Security) out of the 12-month-fees cap (F6), which protects Kaigen's consumer data. Amendment No. 1 dated June 2, 2026, §2, deletes Section 9.2 in its entirety and provides that data security obligations are governed exclusively by the DPA. On its own that looks like housekeeping. DPA §10 makes liability arising under the DPA subject to MSA Section 11, and amendments prevail under MSA §2.3. Read together, the carve-out now points to a section that no longer exists. Dreisur's security failures are DPA breaches, and DPA breaches fall inside the cap. A consumer data breach at Dreisur's warehouse systems would therefore be capped at 12 months of fees.
issues.expected_finding: Because Amendment No. 1 §2 deleted MSA §9.2 and moved data security obligations exclusively into the DPA, whose §10 subjects DPA liability to the MSA cap, the §11.3(b) data security carve-out no longer reaches Dreisur's security breaches, so the carve-out should be restated to cover breaches of the DPA's security obligations.
detect_terms2: Section 9.2 is deleted in its entirety
